historicalTask: Check 1529 Zurich VD16 W2118 vs W2119 typesetting and map later editions to historical manuscript or print copy-text.

verified.finding: Z and K differ in additions at 7/13/15, print W2118 and W2119 separately catalogued, Zwingli Werke 6/2 Nr146 explicitly edited after printed W2119 rather than signed Z.
W2119 original 1529 printed Article15 and Zürich Christoph Froschouer printer colophon visually read in current turn.
V4.65 recorded W2118 original article15 and p7 signatory page, absent printed printer colophon there; source PDF could not be reopened in V4.66, so prior record carried, not independently repeated.
Separate institutional holdings Zwingli MvK A81,8 and 5.174,5 match two 1529 Zurich printed records.

conclusions: V4.65 documented the difference of final printer-colophon between W2118 and W2119; V4.66 reopened W2119 but not W2118.
Distinct catalogue IDs and colophon status cannot alone establish whether the interior pages share typesetting or were re-set.
Edition copy-text is now explicitly mapped: Zwingli Werke 6/2 item146 uses W2119 print, Lutheran 2014 uses K, Reformed Confessions 1/1 item11 uses Z, and MBW Texte 3 item825 uses K plus Z variants.
1610s or modern edited text sources cannot be simply labeled direct Zurich signed manuscript without their independent text-base identity; GHDI WA witness base remains unproven in this research.
